questions.prompt: Henderson frames the course as talks about schools of thought connected to:
choices: B Free markets—various schools converging toward free-market ideas.
C Only economic history of pottery.

questions.prompt: Lectures 1–2 are organized around what he calls:
choices: B The 10 Pillars of Economic Wisdom.

questions.prompt: A corollary of voluntary exchange he stresses is that:
choices: B Both sides gain from an exchange.

questions.prompt: Pillar five highlights that information is:
choices: A Free and centralized in one bureau.
B Valuable and costly—and most valuable information is inherently decentralized.

questions.prompt: Understanding prices helps explain why price controls are destructive: they keep price:
choices: B Below what the market price would be.
C Exactly equal to marginal cost by magic.
